texts: bad: "an apprentice" is read as one particular apprentice, so the parse claims that a single specific apprentice happens to have a large solo count instead of stating the general fact about apprentices, and a possessive subject like "an apprentice's N" has no route into the general form. Rewrite as: "Every apprentice has a large solo count." — an explicit quantifier with a plain verb, which gives every apprentice his or her own large solo count.
good. "the Council" is bound by kind with no name attached, and the verb is left open with the Council as the doer — the shape the translator handles for "what does X do?".
